section: Section 11; Section 15 where repair deductions are relevant
title: Security Deposit and Permitted Deductions
content: The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 is model legislation intended for adoption by States and Union Territories; it does not automatically apply to every tenancy in India. Under Section 11 of the Model Act, the security deposit is agreed in the tenancy agreement subject to the stated statutory caps, and it is to be refunded when vacant possession is taken over after due deduction of liabilities of the tenant. Section 15 also addresses specified repair and maintenance situations in which amounts may be deducted from the security deposit. The applicable State or Union Territory tenancy law and the tenancy agreement must therefore be checked before giving a case-specific answer.
authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
applicability: Do not treat as a universal all-India tenancy rule.
citation: Model Tenancy Act, 2021, Section 11 and relevant Section 15 provisions

act_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Internal Committee, Complaint and Inquiry Process
content: The POSH Act, 2013 provides for an Internal Committee under Section 4 and a complaint mechanism under Section 9. A complaint is ordinarily made within three months from the incident or, in a series of incidents, within three months from the last incident; the Internal Committee may extend this period by up to another three months for reasons recorded in writing. Section 11 governs the inquiry, Section 13 the inquiry report, and Section 19 sets out duties of the employer. The Act should be read together with its rules and the applicable workplace facts.
authority: Ministry of Law and Justice / India Code
applicability: Workplaces covered by the Act; Local Committee provisions may apply where applicable.

title: Consumer Rights and Filing a Complaint
content: Section 2(9) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 defines six consumer rights, including the rights to safety, information, choice, being heard, redressal and consumer awareness. Section 35 provides the mechanism for making a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in the circumstances covered by the Act. The Department of Consumer Affairs also provides official information about electronic filing and consumer grievance mechanisms. The exact relief and forum depend on the facts and applicable jurisdiction.
authority: Department of Consumer Affairs / Legislative Department
applicability: Depends on whether the claimant and transaction fall within the Act.
citation: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(9) and Section 35

topic: Right to Information Request and Timelines
title: RTI Application, Response Period and First Appeal
content: Section 6(1) allows a person to request information under the RTI Act through the prescribed application mechanism. Under Section 7(1), information is ordinarily to be provided within thirty days of receipt of the request, subject to the Act's provisions. Where the information sought concerns the life or liberty of a person, the response period is forty-eight hours. Section 19(1) provides the first-appeal mechanism against a decision of the Central or State Public Information Officer, including where no decision is received within the applicable period.
authority: Ministry of Law and Justice / India Code
applicability: Requests must fall within the RTI Act and its exemptions/procedural requirements.

title: Maternity Benefit and Crèche Provisions
content: The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended, contains provisions on maternity benefit in Section 5 and crèche facilities in Section 11A. For a woman with fewer than two surviving children, Section 5(3) provides a maximum maternity benefit period of twenty-six weeks, subject to the conditions and limits stated in the Act. For a woman with two or more surviving children, the statutory maximum is twelve weeks. Eligibility and application of the Act depend on Section 2 and the facts of the establishment and employee.
authority: Ministry of Law and Justice / India Code
applicability: Subject to the establishments, employees and conditions covered by the Act.

topic: Equal Pay and Wage Payment Rights
title: Gender Non-Discrimination and Wage Payment Timelines
content: Section 3 of the Code on Wages, 2019 prohibits discrimination on the ground of gender in matters relating to wages for the same work or work of a similar nature, subject to the Code's provisions. Section 4 provides for decision-making regarding disputes about whether work is the same or of a similar nature. Section 17 sets time limits for payment of wages; for monthly wages, payment is to be made before expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month, subject to the Code and applicable exceptions. Minimum-wage rules should be retrieved from the relevant provisions rather than inferred from Sections 3 and 4.
authority: Ministry of Law and Justice / India Code
applicability: Subject to the scope and commencement of the Code and applicable rules.

title: Eligibility and Entitlement to Legal Services
content: Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 specifies categories of persons entitled to legal services, including specified socially or legally vulnerable categories and persons meeting the applicable income criterion. Section 13 addresses entitlement after the criteria in Section 12 are satisfied and contains the Act's further conditions. Depending on the case, assistance may be sought through the relevant State Legal Services Authority or District Legal Services Authority.
applicability: Eligibility depends on Section 12 categories, applicable income limits and Section 13 conditions.
citation: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, Sections 12 and 13

act_name: Constitution of India and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
title: Arrest Safeguards, Grounds of Arrest and Magistrate Production
content: Article 22 of the Constitution provides constitutional safeguards concerning arrest and detention, including the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest and the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice, subject to the constitutional exceptions. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is the current central criminal-procedure statute and came into force on 1 July 2024. Its provisions include Section 47 on information as to grounds of arrest and applicable bail information, Section 48 on information about the arrest to a relative, friend or nominated person, and Sections 57 and 58 on taking the arrested person before the appropriate authority and the twenty-four-hour detention limit, subject to the statutory rules and exceptions.
authority: Ministry of Law and Justice / India Code
applicability: Subject to constitutional and statutory exceptions.
citation: Constitution of India, Article 22; BNSS 2023, Sections 47, 48, 57 and 58
